text:
How to source and map XMLTV EPG data for event-based sports channels whose names and IDs change per match?

I'm building a guide (EPG) importer for a live sports application. Channels come from an M3U playlist that is re-fetched on a schedule, and guide data comes from XMLTV. I match the two on tvg-id = XMLTV channel id.

That works for ordinary 24/7 channels. It fails for per-event entries, which make up most of the playlist (about 19,800 entries in about 280 groups, one group per league). A typical entry looks like this:

#EXTINF:-1 tvg-id="" group-title="NBA",NBA 03: Lakers vs Celtics @ 8:00 PM ET

The problems:

tvg-id is empty or reused, and the title changes for every match, so there is no constant key to match against an XMLTV <channel id>.

An entry only carries video around its event, so a linear-style guide with back-to-back programmes doesn't describe it.

XMLTV files I have tested only contain the 24/7 channels, not these per-event entries.

What I have tried:

Matching on tvg-id: only works for the 24/7 channels.

Fuzzy-matching the entry title against XMLTV display-name: too many false matches between similarly named entries.

Parsing team names and start time out of the title with a regex: works until the playlist changes its title format.

My question:

For per-event entries, is it more robust to generate the XMLTV myself from a fixtures schedule (one <programme> per fixture) than to look for them in an existing XMLTV file? If so, what is a reliable way to key a fixture to a playlist entry when the only link is the free-text title?

How to express a conditionally required parameter in a Pydantic-validated tool/API schema, without losing the upfront schema validation?

I have a function (specifically an MCP tool built with FastMCP, but this is really a Pydantic/JSON Schema question) where one parameter is required in the normal case, but must be optional when a separate flag parameter is set, since in that branch it genuinely doesn't apply.

Simplified shape:

async def create_payment_instruction(
    amount: str,
    payment_purpose: PaymentPurpose,       # required normally
    status_check_key: str | None = None,   # when set, payment_purpose is irrelevant
):
    if status_check_key is not None:
        return check_status(status_check_key)
    # payment_purpose must be present from here on

The problem: giving payment_purpose a required type annotation makes the schema reject every call missing it, including the legitimate status-check branch where it's never used. The only fix I've found is making it optional (PaymentPurpose | None = None) and manually checking, inside the function body, that payment_purpose is not None whenever status_check_key is absent.

That works, but now the generated schema (and anything inspecting it, like client-side form generation or docs) reports the field as optional even though it's actually required in the common case. That feels like giving up real validation for a runtime check.

Is there an idiomatic way to express this kind of "required unless field X is set" relationship directly in a Pydantic model, for example with model_validator(mode="after"), a discriminated union, or something in JSON Schema's if/then/dependentRequired, so the constraint is visible in the schema itself rather than only enforced after the fact in the function body?

AWS Glue 6.0 (Spark 4.1) throws No plan for TableReference exception during MERGE INTO operation

I am running into a blocker while executing an Apache Spark MERGE INTO operation in an AWS Glue 6.0 ETL job. The job fails during the query optimization/planning phase with an internal developer assertion error.

Environment details:

AWS Glue Version: 6.0 (which ships with AWS-optimized Apache Spark 4.1.1)

Language: PySpark / Spark SQL

Operation: Standard MERGE INTO target USING source ON ... WHEN MATCHED ...

error:

org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.errors.package$TreeNodeException: No plan for TableReference
  at org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.errors.package$.attachTree(package.scala:56)
  ...
  Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchElementException: No plan for TableReference
  at org.apache.spark.sql.execution.SparkPlanner.org$apache$spark$sql$execution$SparkPlanner$$plan(SparkPlanner.scala:62)

What is causing this:

After digging through open-source tracker reports, this appears to be a known Catalyst optimizer bug introduced in the Spark 4.1.x line.

When the optimizer runs its evaluation rules, if a source relation or filtered step evaluates or resolves down to an empty local relation plan structure before physical execution, the MERGE INTO processing logic completely breaks down.

This bug is reportedly fixed in Spark 4.2, but because AWS Glue 6.0 hardcodes the Spark 4.1 runtime environment, I cannot manually upgrade or patch the underlying Spark framework version.

I tried via disabling adaptive.sql but the error persists no matter what.. Is there any way to bypass this while staying on Glue 6.0?
